# Preface {.unnumbered}

This is the slow, linear version of the material in my
[notes](https://neilshahcosmos.com/notes/): an attempt to write down, in the order I
wish I had learned it, the group theory and representation theory that a
physicist needs in order to read quantum field theory with understanding rather
than faith.

The intended reader is me a year ago — someone with a physics background, a
working knowledge of calculus and linear algebra, and a growing suspicion that
the phrase "transforms as a spinor" is hiding a precise mathematical statement.
It is. The aim of this book is to make such statements precise without losing
the physical motivation that makes them worth caring about.

## What this book is and is not

It is a set of notes, not a textbook. Proofs are given when they contain an idea
and sketched when they are bookkeeping. Examples are chosen for their relevance
to physics: the dihedral groups appear because molecules have them, $\SU(2)$
appears early and often because spin exists, and the Lorentz group is the
destination of the whole first half.

It is not a substitute for the real references, which are cited throughout and
collected in the [bibliography](references.qmd). In particular, Artin
[@artin2011] for algebra, Hall [@hall2015] for Lie theory, and Woit
[@woit2017] for the connection to quantum mechanics are the books this one
leans on most.

## Conventions

Groups are written multiplicatively with identity $e$ unless they are obviously
additive. Matrix groups are written $\GL(n,\C)$, $\SU(2)$, and so on; their Lie
algebras in fraktur, $\gl(n,\C)$, $\su(2)$. Physicists' conventions are used for
Hermitian generators and the factor of $i$ in $U = e^{-i\theta T}$; the
mathematicians' convention is noted wherever the two collide. The Minkowski
metric is mostly-minus, $\eta = \diag(+,-,-,-)$.

## Status

The book is being written in public. Chapters appear as they stabilise; the
corresponding [notes](https://neilshahcosmos.com/notes/) usually come first and are
rougher. Corrections are welcome.
